newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds factor in US hike possibility.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds factor in US hike possibility.

text.p: *Australian bonds ended softer amid mild profit-taking as the market showed some caution ahead of the FOMC meeting next Tuesday, where a U.S. rate hike remains a possibility.
*Spreads to the U.S. wind back after recent tightening.
Australian bonds ended softer amid mild profit-taking after a week that saw domestic supply and generally weak U.S. bonds failing to make much of an impression on a bullish local market.

Traders said investors were finally showing some caution ahead of the Federal Open Market Committe meeting next Tuesday, an event that has gripped the U.S. debt market for some weeks as it debated the 'will they, won't they' possibility of tightening in monetary policy.
"This has been a classic case of pre-weekend profit-taking, and it's not surprising with the FOMC coming up," one added.

The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread had narrowed to around 106 basis points in after hours trading on Thursday, its lowest level in over two years, as the market continued to show resilience to a fragile U.S. market.

However, it failed to maintain the break below 110 basis points as profit-takers stepped in, although analysts remain fairly positive that the local market can ride out any storm if the Fed does tighten given current domestic fundamentals.
Meanwhile, the local market will have little new data to work week next week, although new RBA governor Ian Macfarlane will be speaking to a conference in Canberra on Wednesday.

The slight local retracement saw the market generally underperforming other dollar bloc bonds at the close. Canadian bonds had firmed on Thursday in a thin market, while New Zealand debt continued to rebound after its recent weakness, albeit closing below the day's highs.
The minor retracement on the 10-year bond futures contract saw a two-week upward trendline broken at 92.040, but support was seen on a test of 92.000.
